reading.title: Morning Traffic
reading.text: Every morning the main road in our town is full of cars and buses. The rush-hour traffic is so heavy that a short trip can take forty minutes. Last Monday my father was stuck in a traffic jam because the traffic lights were broken. A traffic warden stood at the corner and showed drivers when to go. The noise was terrible, but nobody was angry. The mayor says the city wants to reduce traffic congestion by building a new bus lane. I hope it works, because I would like to arrive at school on time.

listening.title: Late for School
listening.script: Ali: Sorry I am late, Miss. There was a lot of traffic on the way. Teacher: Was there an accident? Ali: No, only heavy traffic. The traffic lights near the market were not working, and we were stuck for twenty minutes. Teacher: I see. Next time, please leave ten minutes earlier. Ali: Yes, I will. My mother says the rush-hour traffic is worse on Mondays. Teacher: Quite true. Now please sit down and open your book.

reading.title: My Street
reading.text: I live on a quiet street at the edge of the town. Our street is narrow, with old trees on both sides. At the end of the street there is a small market where people sell fruit and bread. On Saturdays a street musician plays the guitar near the corner, and the neighbours stop to listen. In the evening the street lamps come on, and children play in the street until their mothers call them. Last year the council wanted to turn it into a busy one-way street, but we signed a letter and kept it peaceful.

reading.title: Lost in the Old Town
reading.text: Last summer we visited the old town of Khiva. We had a street map, but the narrow lanes made it hard to follow our route. At one corner, we got lost and could not find the main gate. My sister looked at the map again and saw that we had taken the wrong turn. A friendly shopkeeper pointed to the shortest route back and told us about a scenic route along the old wall. We followed it and saw the sunset over the towers. In the end, getting lost was the best part of the day.

reading.title: A Lucky Escape
reading.text: Yesterday afternoon I witnessed an accident near our school. A small car turned the corner too fast, and a boy on a bike had to stop suddenly. Luckily the driver braked in time, so there was only a minor accident. The boy fell off his bike, but he stood up and said he was fine. A teacher called the police to report the accident, and a doctor checked the boy to be safe. Everyone agreed that accidents happen quickly, and that slower driving can avoid many of them. Today the school put up a new traffic sign near the gate.

listening.script: Officer: Good morning, children. Today I want to talk about road accidents. Most accidents happen because drivers or walkers are not careful. Wear a helmet on your bike. Accident prevention is simple, and it starts with you. Now, does anyone have a question?

reading.text: Every Saturday Tarik plays football for his school team. Last month he suffered a knee injury during an important match. He did gentle exercises every day to recover from the injury. This Saturday he is allowed to play again. He says he will warm up carefully to prevent another sports injury.
